extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, scientists, and philosophers concerned with method and the cultivation of right understanding
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how to investigate nature and construct sound philosophy: avoid systematic errors ('idols'), use experiments and careful induction, and evaluate theories by their fruits and progress rather than authority. Emphasizes purification of the understanding and methodical experimentation aimed at causes and axioms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid factions of ancients and moderns
rubrics_metrics.description: Some dispositions evince an unbounded admiration of antiquity, others eagerly embrace novelty; truth is not to be sought in the good fortune of any particular conjuncture of time but in the light of nature and experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not judge theories by whether they are ancient or modern. Reject party zeal for the ancients or moderns; instead seek truth in nature and experience which are 'eternal.' Avoid letting temporal authority or fashion determine assent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate attention between particulars and generals
rubrics_metrics.description: The contemplation of nature in individual form distracts and weakens; contemplation of general composition stupefies and relaxes. These two species of contemplation must be interchanged and each employed in its turn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To render the understanding both penetrating and capacious, alternate detailed observation of particulars with study of general structure; this prevents extremes of over-discrimination and over-generalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspect what especially fixes your understanding (Idols of the den)
rubrics_metrics.description: Such precautions in contemplation will ward off and expel the idols of the den, which owe their birth to predominant pursuits, excess in synthesis/analysis, party zeal, or the extent/narrowness of the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be alert to the biases produced by your own natural disposition, occupation, or habitual focus; when something 'takes and fixes' your understanding, exercise extra caution to keep judgment even and unprejudiced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware idols of the market: words and names can mislead
rubrics_metrics.description: The idols of the market are those which have entwined themselves round the understanding from the associations of words and names; men imagine reason governs words while words react upon the understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disputes often terminate in controversies about words; imitate mathematicians by defining terms carefully. Because definitions themselves are verbal, rely also on particular instances and orderly series/arrangements to determine notions and axioms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish two kinds of word-based idols
rubrics_metrics.description: Idols imposed by words are of two kinds: names of things which have no existence (fictitious concepts), or names of actual objects but confused, badly defined, and hastily and irregularly abstracted from things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminate fictitious names by refutation and disuse of their theories; treat confused abstractions as more deeply rooted and requiring careful analysis of meanings and instances to correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize degrees of distortion in words (which concepts are more faulty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Names of substances (less abstract species) are least faulty; words signifying actions are more faulty; the most faulty are those denoting qualities (except immediate objects of sense) like 'heavy' and 'light.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer clearer, less abstract terms when possible; when using abstract quality-terms, be aware they often conflate different senses and require verification by instances and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject idols of the theatre: beware dogmatic systems and sophistical demonstrations
rubrics_metrics.description: The idols of the theatre are instilled by the fictions of theories and depraved rules of demonstration; many systems are founded on disputation rather than nature and experiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept theories because they form elegant systems or persuasive demonstrations. Level wit and intellect with method: reduce reliance on rhetorical or sectarian argument and give precedence to methodical investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid empiricism built on too few experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: The empiric school forms dogmas from the confined obscurity of a few experiments; such philosophy appears certain to those practiced in such experiments but is futile to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not generalize from a small set of experiments. Extend inquiry beyond narrow, repeated focus on one phenomenon (e.g., alchemy, magnetism) and guard against premature generalization from idiosyncratic experimental contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep theology and superstition separate from natural philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Corruption of philosophy by mixing it with superstition and theology leads to fanciful doctrines and the apotheosis of error; some have tried to build natural philosophy on Scripture, which is inappropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise greatest caution to prevent theological or superstitious concepts from shaping natural-philosophical inquiry. Keep matters of faith and matters of natural investigation distinct to avoid corrupting both.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose proper subjects for contemplation: prefer active principles and intermediate objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Erroneous focus on mechanical arts or on primary/elementary forms leads to fiction (elements, occult properties); physicians and investigators should consider secondary qualities and the operations (attraction, repulsion, attenuation, etc.); prefer active causes over stationary principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concentrate on investigating observable operations and intermediate, useful phenomena rather than chasing ultimate atoms or shapeless matter. Study tendencies (adhesion, return to natural dimensions, congregation) and secondary/operative qualities which yield practical knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid intemperance in assent: neither dogmatic certainty nor boundless skepticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Excesses are of two kinds: deciding hastily and rendering sciences positive and dictatorial, or introducing scepticism and vague unbounded inquiry; the former subdues, the latter enervates understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain balanced judgment: favor honest probabilistic doctrines over arbitrary decision, but avoid despairing of discovering truth. Provide assistance to weak senses and understanding by method rather than yielding to either extreme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purge the understanding of idols (moral of purification)
rubrics_metrics.description: All kinds of idols must be abjured and renounced with firm and solemn resolution so the understanding may be completely freed and cleared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a deliberate program of intellectual purification—identify, abjure, and correct idols (of the den, market, theatre, and tribe) to clear the path to knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware fourfold defects in the ordinary demonstrative process
rubrics_metrics.description: The process leading from senses and things to axioms and conclusions is fallacious in four equal parts: (1) impressions of the senses are erroneous; (2) notions are improperly abstracted and indeterminate; (3) induction employed is improper, relying on simple enumeration; (4) the usual method of establishing most general propositions first and deducing particulars is the parent of error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct scientific method by addressing each defect: improve sensory correction/substitution, refine abstraction practices to produce determinate notions, develop proper inductive methods beyond mere enumeration (with exclusions/resolutions), and reform the order of discovery away from premature generalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use experience as demonstration only when strictly adhered to the experiment
rubrics_metrics.description: Experience is by far the best demonstration provided it adhere to the experiment actually made; transferring an experiment to other subjects without methodical caution becomes fallacious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make experiments methodical, extensive, and aimed at eliciting causes and axioms (seeking light rather than immediate profit). Avoid casual, haphazard experimentation and premature turn to practice; build axioms from systematic experimental inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge philosophies by external signs: origin, fruits, progress, author confessions, and unanimity/dissent
rubrics_metrics.description: External signs of weakness include origin (e.g., Greek origin that is professional/disputatious), the character of the age, the fruits produced (practical discoveries), the increase/progress of a system, confessions of its authors about obscurity/limits, and dissension or supposed unanimity among adherents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate doctrines by practical results ('fruits') and growth: systems founded on nature will grow and produce useful arts; those founded on opinion will stagnate. Regard unanimous acceptance with suspicion (unanimity often stems from prejudice/authority). Consider authorial confessions of difficulty as a sign of limitation rather than finality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize historical and contextual causes of entrenched error
rubrics_metrics.description: The causes of errors and their long perseverance are numerous: limited historical knowledge, small geographic understanding, professional and disputatious character of prior thinkers, and social/institutional factors that favored certain systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing entrenched doctrines, take into account historical constraints and sociocultural incentives that sustained them; understanding these causes helps explain persistence of error and guides reform of method.
